title: Tôi cần nước
summary: Different ways to say "I need water" in Vietnam, with the safe phrase, reusable pieces, and nearby next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Use this when drinking water or rinse water is the immediate need. This covers both bathroom and personal-need moments where you just need water fast. Start with the full phrase, then use the nearby rows when the conversation needs one more step.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Use the cards to hear the phrase in pieces, then listen to the full version so the rhythm stays connected.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Tôi cần nước is the safest default for "I need water". Use this when drinking water or rinse water is the immediate need. Say it slowly, then point, show your phone, or hold up the item if the other person needs more context.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use this when drinking water or rinse water is the immediate need. Use it in bathrooms, soap, paper, water, and basic personal needs when one clear sentence will work better than a long explanation.

sections.title: Watch out
sections.body: Some places may not have paper or soap available. Asking early avoids an awkward surprise.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: Ask directly and follow gestures. People may simply point you toward the right place.
